result.summary: Mark all database read, write, erase, and transaction operations in WalletBatch and CWallet::WriteBestBlock as [[nodiscard]]. Update all callers across the wallet subsystem to either handle returned errors, surface failure results, or explicitly cast them to void with an explanatory comment.
result.problem: Wallet database write and erase failures were frequently ignored across the codebase. When database operations fail silently, in-memory state can diverge from persistent on-disk records (such as address indices, transaction records, or address book entries), risking wallet corruption, desynchronization, or data loss.
evidence: PR description: 'A common theme in the wallet is that many database write failures are ignored, when they should probably be handled, or at least documented that a failure is being ignored.'
Commit 5b35156ed6: 'All WalletBatch operations that interact with the database (read, write, erase, transactions) have bool returns values that callers need to check as database operations may fail.'
result.scope_notes: Touches database write call sites across wallet core, SPKM, migration, and export logic.
result.card: This pull request marks all database interaction methods in WalletBatch as nodiscard and updates callers across the wallet to handle failures or explicitly document ignored errors. Previously, callers frequently ignored write failures silently, allowing in-memory state (such as key generation indices, transaction state updates, and address book metadata) to diverge from persistent disk records without alerting the user. Failure handling now halts or surfaces errors during address generation, loading, wallet export, and wallet migration. The previously required dependency for encryption state updates (#35752) has merged.

risk.why: Unintended early returns or thrown exceptions on database write failures could cause unexpected wallet operation aborts or rollbacks.
